clue.text: Nothing in Vogue? Florence finds shift

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside the others, here Florence's short name going into nothing plus vogue

parts.note: a vogue is a craze or fad
Flo is the short form of the name Florence

explanation.surface: Someone notices that Florence is not featured in Vogue magazine and decides to move on.
explanation.walkthrough: Florence's short name sits inside the other two pieces, splitting them; 'finds' is just a link joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To offload a burden is to move or unload it, which is what shifting something means.

clue.text: Cherry beer drinker, probably, in a radio drama

definitions.text: Cherry beer drinker, probably, in a radio drama

parts.words: Cherry beer drinker, probably, in a radio drama
parts.note: the clue describes a Welsh villager from Dylan Thomas's radio play Under Milk Wood whose first name is Cherry and who drinks heavily

explanation.walkthrough: Cherry is a first name, not a fruit: Cherry Owen, the hard-drinking villager in Dylan Thomas's radio play Under Milk Wood.
explanation.definitionFit: In Under Milk Wood the boozy character is called Cherry by first name and this by surname.

clue.text: A defender, carrying a small torch, is rejected in this play on wartime romance

indicators.note: something rejected is thrown back, so in this down clue the letters are read backwards
carrying means one word holds another inside it

parts.note: a half or half-back is a defensive position in football and rugby
a taper is a thin candle or wick used as a small torch

explanation.surface: A footballing defender holding a small torch is turned away, in a play about wartime love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is rejected' turns the whole build round, which suits a down clue. Terence Rattigan's play is set at an RAF bomber station.
explanation.definitionFit: Terence Rattigan's 1942 stage play of that title tells a love triangle at an RAF airfield in the war.

clue.text: Poem with lines on Murdoch's printing works manager

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem
L is the abbreviation for line, so LL means lines

explanation.surface: A verse with a few lines written about a newspaper tycoon's print-shop boss.
explanation.walkthrough: Murdoch suggests the press baron, but here it points to a character of that name in a Murdoch novel.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue names a minor character by his job in a novel, a common literary-crossword device.

clue.text: Arthur Koestler's "Number One" best seller?

parts.note: Koestler's famous novel of Stalin's purges features a dictator called simply Number One, and the book sold hugely

explanation.walkthrough: Number One is the Stalin figure in Koestler's novel, but the quoted phrase also reads as a chart-topping best seller.
explanation.definitionFit: Koestler's 1940 novel about a revolutionary imprisoned and tried by the Party bears this title.

clue.text: Quickly possibly seen in Victor's effective opening in bard production

indicators.note: seen in signals that Victor and an opening letter are placed inside the reworked word bard
a production of something stages it afresh, so the word bard is rearranged

parts.note: Victor is V in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A powerful start by someone called Victor in a staging of Shakespeare.
explanation.walkthrough: BARD rearranged gives ADRB, with V and E (the first letter of 'effective') set inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Quickly is an example of a word modifying a verb, the part of speech this names.

clue.text: Truth possibly, or an attempt to get close to it on stage

definitions.text: Truth possibly, or an attempt to get close to it on stage

parts.words: Truth possibly, or an attempt to get close to it on stage
parts.note: a dramatised retelling of real events is a stage or screen attempt to approach the truth

explanation.walkthrough: The clue plays on drama based on fact: a performance that only approximates what really happened.
explanation.definitionFit: A genre of drama that reconstructs actual events, blending documentary with fiction.

clue.text: In the final part of TOWIE, Tracey is someone playing a smallpart

annotationWithheld.why: In the final part of TOWIE, Tracey is someone playing a smallpart (5): EXTRA is hidden in ESSEX TRACEY, but Essex is only implied by TOWIE (The Only Way Is Essex), so hid() over printed words cannot express it
annotationWithheld.clue: In the final part of TOWIE, Tracey is someone playing a smallpart

clue.text: Caribbean-based novel from Hardy, with limbo dancing

indicators.note: dancing has the letters of Hardy and limbo jig about into a new order

explanation.surface: A novel from Thomas Hardy set in the West Indies, complete with limbo dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: Hardy suggests Thomas Hardy, but this is Margaret Atwood's 1981 novel, set on a Caribbean island.
explanation.definitionFit: Margaret Atwood's novel follows a Canadian journalist caught up in political upheaval on a Caribbean island.

clue.text: Eccentric adoring Helena? That's about right for this Trollope character

indicators.note: about means the jumbled letters go around the abbreviation for right
eccentric means odd, so the letters of adoring Helena are put in an odd order

explanation.surface: An odd person devoted to Helena gets a mention for one of Trollope's people.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram wraps round R; 'That's' is a link. She is Mr Harding's daughter in Trollope's The Warden.
explanation.definitionFit: The warden's younger daughter in Trollope's Barchester novels, who later marries Mr Arabin.

clue.text: Part of opera's easy to cut

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some of an opera is simple to trim.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut a passage from a text is to delete or strike it out.

clue.text: Moved by adaptation, do Electra

indicators.note: an adaptation reworks a play, so the letters of do Electra are reordered

explanation.surface: A theatregoer is moved by a new adaptation of the Greek tragedy Electra.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moved' reads as touched emotionally, but it means shifted to a new place.
explanation.definitionFit: Something relocated has been shifted to a new site, a synonym of moved.

clue.text: Slope's linked with loss of power in this novel

parts.note: a slope is a decline, a downward incline
and is the joining word, the link
a fall is a loss of power, as with a government's fall

explanation.surface: A hillside joined to a collapse in strength makes up a well-known book.
explanation.walkthrough: Slope might suggest Trollope's Obadiah Slope, but here it is a downward incline. The novel is Evelyn Waugh's first.
explanation.definitionFit: Evelyn Waugh's 1928 satirical novel about Paul Pennyfeather bears this title, borrowed from Gibbon.

clue.text: Schoolboy's challenge about a mistake made with one Romeo

indicators.note: about means the dare goes around the other pieces

parts.note: a dare is a challenge
bish is British slang for a mistake or blunder
one is I, the Roman numeral
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A schoolboy's dare goes wrong when a mistake is made with a boy called Romeo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Schoolboy's' reads 'schoolboy is': the answer is Jennings's best friend in Anthony Buckeridge's school stories. BISH is British slang for a blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: Jennings's bespectacled best friend in Buckeridge's boarding-school stories is a classic fictional pupil.

clue.text: Mutineers cunning one's embraced

indicators.note: embraced means one piece holds another inside it

parts.note: one is AN, and the possessive gives S
arch means sly or cunning

explanation.surface: Rebels on board have been taken in by a sly crewman.
explanation.walkthrough: Arch in the sense of sly or knowing, as in an arch smile, not the curved structure.
explanation.definitionFit: Anarchs are leaders of revolt or rebellion, like those who rise against a ship's captain.

clue.text: "The winter wind is loud and wild, / - to me, my darling child" (Emily Brontë)

definitions.text: "The winter wind is loud and wild, / - to me, my darling child" (Emily Brontë)

parts.words: "The winter wind is loud and wild, / - to me, my darling child" (Emily Brontë)
parts.note: the missing words in Emily Brontë's poem are a mother's invitation to draw near

explanation.walkthrough: A fill-in-the-blank quotation: the missing words complete the line from Emily Brontë's poem.
explanation.definitionFit: The gap in the poem is a call to draw near, matching the phrase meaning approach.

clue.text: Slope's severe — one between zero and a height

indicators.note: between means a piece is placed inside, flanked by the others

parts.note: zero is the letter O
bad means severe, as in a bad cold
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: Someone's slope is steep, with a single point between ground level and a high one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slope's' reads 'Slope is': Mr Slope, the oily chaplain in Trollope's Barchester Towers, has this first name.
explanation.definitionFit: The scheming chaplain in Barchester Towers is named Obadiah Slope, so his first name fits.

clue.text: MP is found shifting heaps of dope

indicators.note: shifting moves the letters of MP is found about into a new order

explanation.surface: A politician is caught moving piles of drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dope' is information, not drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Dope is slang for information, and these are large piles of it delivered at once.

clue.text: Strand's surprising location in a Shakespeare play

definitions.text: Strand's surprising location in a Shakespeare play

parts.words: Strand's surprising location in a Shakespeare play
parts.note: in The Winter's Tale a ship lands on a coast in a landlocked kingdom, so a strand or shore is famously out of place

explanation.walkthrough: Strand suggests the London street, but means a shore: The Winter's Tale gives this landlocked kingdom a seacoast.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Winter's Tale gives this central European kingdom a seacoast it never had.

clue.text: "Cats have no souls (..). The most majestic cat in the universe would balance a carrot on his — a bite of pork liver." (Philip K. Dick)

definitions.text: "Cats have no souls (..). The most majestic cat in the universe would balance a carrot on his — a bite of pork liver." (Philip K. Dick)

parts.words: "Cats have no souls (..). The most majestic cat in the universe would balance a carrot on his — a bite of pork liver." (Philip K. Dick)
parts.note: the missing words in Philip K. Dick's quip give a body part followed by a word for in exchange

explanation.walkthrough: A fill-in-the-blank quotation: the gap is completed by a body part and a preposition, reading as a phrase meaning 'make for'.
explanation.definitionFit: The words fit the quotation, and together they also form a phrase meaning go towards.

clue.text: Horrible events may be reported in this distressing scene with angry date

definitions.text: Horrible events may be reported in this

indicators.note: distressing suggests the letters of scene angry date are knocked out of shape

explanation.surface: An upsetting scene with a cross partner on a night out.
explanation.walkthrough: In tragedy modelled on Seneca, violent deeds are usually narrated by messengers rather than shown, hence 'reported'.
explanation.definitionFit: Plays in the Roman Seneca's style feature bloody crimes recounted by messengers offstage.

clue.text: A newspaper employee in general (despite his title) is not well off

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: Michel Ney was one of Napoleon's commanders
ED is short for editor, a newspaper employee

explanation.surface: A journalist who is a general by name is still poor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Despite his title' notes that Ney held the rank of Marshal of France, not simply general; those words add colour only.
explanation.definitionFit: Being needy means lacking money, the state of someone not well off.

clue.text: Famous singer left Italy after a show

indicators.note: after means these letters come following the show

parts.note: a gig is a show or performance
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: A celebrated vocalist departs Italy once the concert is over.
explanation.walkthrough: Beniamino Gigli was an Italian operatic tenor.
explanation.definitionFit: Beniamino Gigli was a celebrated Italian tenor of the twentieth century.

clue.text: The beginning of H. Rider Haggard's literary output

definitions.text: The beginning of H. Rider Haggard's literary output

parts.words: The beginning of H. Rider Haggard's literary output
parts.note: the start of a day, and also the title of Haggard's first novel of 1884

explanation.walkthrough: The beginning reads as daybreak and also names Haggard's first novel, published in 1884.
explanation.definitionFit: The word for daybreak, a beginning, was also the title of Haggard's debut novel.

clue.text: Chinua Achebe's editor, one with a general sulkiness about society

parts.note: Ike was the nickname of General Eisenhower

indicators.note: about puts the sulkiness around the abbreviation for society

parts.note: a mood is a fit of sulkiness
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A Nigerian writer's editor sulks over society in the company of a general.
explanation.walkthrough: He is the newspaper editor in Achebe's Anthills of the Savannah, not Achebe's real editor.
explanation.definitionFit: In Anthills of the Savannah, this poet runs the National Gazette, the state newspaper.

clue.text: Good book by Jane Austen, or one by Noel Streatfield

parts.note: Emma is one of Jane Austen's novels

explanation.surface: A fine Austen novel, or else one by the children's author Streatfeild.
explanation.walkthrough: Noel Streatfeild, author of Ballet Shoes, wrote a children's novel of this title in 1968.
explanation.definitionFit: Streatfeild wrote a novel with this girl's name as its title, about a young actress.

clue.text: French palace with two seats for bishops

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city, the seat of a bishop
a see is a bishop's seat or diocese

explanation.surface: A grand French residence furnished with a pair of thrones for clergy.
explanation.walkthrough: Ely is an English cathedral city; the palace is the French president's residence.
explanation.definitionFit: The Paris residence of the French president is known by this name.

clue.text: Cookery writer at last giving equipment to her child

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of the word giving

parts.note: a rig is a set of equipment
a son is a child

explanation.surface: A cook finally hands over her kit to her son.
explanation.walkthrough: Jane Grigson, the English food writer, was succeeded in the trade by her daughter Sophie.
explanation.definitionFit: Jane Grigson was a celebrated English food writer, and her daughter Sophie followed her.
